name: xAI GPU SPV (Colossus 2 chip-leasing vehicle)
monetization: Special-purpose vehicle that buys Nvidia GPUs and leases them to xAI over five years; monetizes via lease payments, keeping ~$20B of compute financing — and the hardware — off xAI's balance sheet.
description_md: The xAI GPU SPV is the ~$20B financing vehicle reported in October 2025 as part of xAI's expanded fundraising for the Colossus 2 data center in Memphis. Structure: ~$7.5B of equity anchored by Valor Equity Partners (including up to $2B from Nvidia itself) plus up to ~$12.5B of GPU-backed debt led by Apollo Global Management and Diameter Capital Partners. The SPV purchases Nvidia chips and leases them back to xAI over five years in a lease-to-own arrangement with a buyout option; Valor subsequently raised ~$5.4B toward the equity anchor.
ai_monetization_md: Cash in: equity from Valor/Nvidia/co-investors and secured debt from Apollo/Diameter-led lenders. Cash out: GPU purchases from Nvidia. Cash back: five-year lease payments from xAI. Two-sided accounting: the SPV owns the assets and carries the financing, while xAI records only an operating expense — no debt and no depreciating GPU fleet on xAI's balance sheet. Lenders' recovery is designed to come from the hardware itself rather than xAI's corporate credit. Nvidia's ≤$2B equity participation means the chip vendor holds equity in the vehicle whose sole purpose is buying its chips (`vendor_financing` / `equity_for_revenue` pattern).
risk_notes_md: This is the cleanest live example of `collateralized_gpu_debt`: the collateral (used GB300-generation GPUs) is priced off the same AI demand cycle that determines xAI's ability to pay its leases — wrong-way risk by construction, and nobody has established what a repossessed 5-year-old GPU fleet is worth at this scale. The five-year lease term itself embeds a useful-life assumption that is contested (the Burry depreciation debate). Counterparty risk shifted in February 2026 when xAI merged into SpaceX — a stronger consolidated credit, but lease obligations' priority within the merged entity is undisclosed. Precise SPV legal structure, lessor identity, and covenant terms have not been made public.

observations.notes: ~$7.5B equity + up to $12.5B GPU-backed debt; sized for Nvidia chips for Colossus 2 (Memphis).
Nvidia contribution capped around $2B — the chip vendor as equity holder in its own demand.
'Up to' figure; secured by the GPUs so lenders recover through hardware rather than xAI's credit.

events.title: ~$20B GPU-leasing SPV structure reported, with Nvidia equity backing
events.why_it_matters: Landmark test of GPUs as standalone loan collateral and of off-balance-sheet compute for a frontier lab — the structure Nvidia's Aug 2026 coalition later sought to generalize.

events.title: Lessee xAI merges into SpaceX
events.why_it_matters: The SPV's sole counterparty became part of a ~$1.25T combined entity — changing the credit behind the leases without any public disclosure of how obligations rank in the merged company.
